- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.0 to -0.2) triggers downward correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days, then adjust to trend.
- If model forecast is >15% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–1.0% per day for next 5 days.
